key_insight: Layer-wise generalizations of Barron norms characterize expected discretization error when converting infinite-width layers into finite neural networks.
engineering_relevance: The theory offers a framework for allocating finite network capacity across layers to control approximation error.
method: Separate approximation into selecting optimal infinite-width layers and discretizing them into finite layers.
Characterize expected discretization error using layer-wise Barron norms.
Analyze local minima through an equidistribution principle analogous to adaptive spline and finite element approximation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical characterizations of discretization error and local minima, but no datasets, benchmarks, or numerical results.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish a practical algorithm for finding optimal infinite-width layers or globally optimal finite networks.
paper_title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
